proposal.root_problem: Customers experience indefinite waits for refund resolution because a subset of refund transactions in DA-PAY fail at payment processing with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT and never complete, not because support lacks a self-service answer channel or because agents are slow to respond (median ticket response is 2.0h against a 24h SLA) (E-01, E-02).
proposal.requested_solution: Build a chatbot so customers get instant answers about refund status (requester framing, SH-SUP, CL-01/CL-02).
symptoms: Customers report waiting a long time for answers about refund status (CL-01, CL-02, E-03).
5 refund records in payment-db are stuck in FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT status (E-01).
Ticket response times are well within SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h, 900 tickets) (E-02).
causal_chain: Customer submits a refund that is processed against DA-PAY.
The refund's IBAN data is in an invalid format, so payment-db processing rejects it with status FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT (E-01).
Because the refund never completes, there is no resolved refund status for the customer to receive.
Customer opens or escalates a support ticket asking about the refund.
Support agents respond within SLA (median 2.0h vs 24h, E-02) but cannot report completion because the underlying payment is still failed.
Customer experiences this as 'waiting forever' even though ticket handling itself is fast.

assumptions.statement: The 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records returned by payment-db.refund_failures are assumed to represent the refund failures driving the current complaint, not a partial sample of a larger problem.
The 900 tickets measured in E-02 are assumed to include the refund-related tickets behind the complaint, so the within-SLA finding generalizes to refund tickets.
FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT status is assumed to mean the refund cannot complete without data correction (not quickly auto-retried), making it the source of the indefinite wait.

key_points: Problem as defined (PD-1): customers experience indefinite waits for refund resolution because a subset of refund transactions in DA-PAY fail at payment processing with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT status and never complete — not because support lacks a self-service channel or agents respond slowly (E-01, E-02).

The requester's original framing (SH-SUP, CL-01/CL-02) was that a chatbot was needed because customers wait forever for answers; this hypothesis (H-CHATBOT-NEEDED) was REJECTED, contradicted by E-01 and E-02.

Supporting evidence: E-01 (payment-db.refund_failures) returned 5 refund records, all FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT; E-02 (ticket-db.response_times) showed median ticket response of 2.0h against a 24h SLA across 900 tickets, i.e. support response was not the bottleneck.

Hypothesis H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURE was CONFIRMED (supported by E-01, E-02); H-AGENT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE and H-SYSTEM-FRAGMENTATION were REJECTED (contradicted by E-02); H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING remains an open CANDIDATE, deferred as VOB-U-PROCESSING-SPEED-VS-FORMAT.
DEFINE gate result was CONDITIONAL_PASS, with the HIGH-criticality unknown U-PROCESSING-SPEED-VS-FORMAT deferred to a verification obligation (VOB) rather than resolved.

What was released (release decision: RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION, no items on hold): the investigation deliverable packaging the already-run payment-db refund_failures results (investigate_iban_failures:DA-PAY, work item W-WI-1, DONE) and the ticket response-time monitoring deliverable (monitor_ticket_response_times:DA-TCK, work item W-WI-2, DONE).

Actual remediation of the refund failures — correct_iban_format_data and reprocess_failed_refunds — was NOT released: these actions sit outside the release scope and remain blocked by VOB-R-2 and VOB-U-PROCESSING-SPEED-VS-FORMAT, both still OPEN, plus no write access and no confirmed handoff recipient.

Open conflicts (C-1, C-2, C-3) remain unresolved between the chatbot-cause claims (CL-01, CL-02, E-03) and the IBAN-failure evidence (E-01); these do not block the released investigation/monitoring scope.
limitations_explained: The DEFINE gate only reached CONDITIONAL_PASS, meaning some items were deferred as verification obligations (VOBs) rather than fully resolved before release.

VOB-U-PROCESSING-SPEED-VS-FORMAT (whether slow intrinsic processing also contributes to the wait, H-SLOW-REFUND-PROCESSING) is still OPEN, but it blocks only the correct/reprocess actions, which are outside this release's scope.
VOB-R-2 (who holds confirmed write authority over DA-PAY to execute the correction/reprocessing) is still OPEN; it also only blocks actions outside this release's scope.

VOB-R-3, which does intersect the released investigation scope, is non-critical: it asks whether the 5 known FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records (E-01) represent the full scale of failures or whether unobserved failure modes exist in DA-PAY (U-FAILURE-VOLUME-SCALE, OPEN).
Ticket response time (E-02) staying within the 24h SLA confirms response speed was never the bottleneck, but this does not address the refund-completion delay itself.
The 5 FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT records in E-01 may not represent the full failure volume; U-FAILURE-VOLUME-SCALE remains OPEN and unresolved.
SC-COMPLETION-DURATION-TARGET has no defined threshold because baseline refund completion duration data does not yet exist, so measurable success for completion duration cannot be assessed.

This environment has no write access to payment-db, so correct_iban_format_data and reprocess_failed_refunds could not be executed; and no stakeholder/organization has confirmed write authority over DA-PAY (domain_authorizations is empty), so no handoff recipient for that remediation work has been identified.
proposal.summary: The problem was defined (PD-1) as: customers wait indefinitely for refund resolution because a subset of DA-PAY refund transactions fail at payment processing with FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT status and never complete — not because of a missing self-service channel or slow agent response, as originally claimed by the requester SH-SUP (CL-01, CL-02). This was established via payment-db evidence E-01 (5 refund records, all FAILED_IBAN_FORMAT) and ticket-db evidence E-02 (median response 2.0h vs 24h SLA across 900 tickets), which together confirmed H-IBAN-FORMAT-FAILURE and rejected H-CHATBOT-NEEDED, H-AGENT-CAPACITY-SHORTAGE, and H-SYSTEM-FRAGMENTATION. The DEFINE gate reached only CONDITIONAL_PASS, deferring the HIGH-criticality unknown of whether intrinsic processing speed also contributes (U-PROCESSING-SPEED-VS-FORMAT) to a verification obligation. The release decision is RELEASE_WITH_KNOWN_LIMITATION (nothing held back entirely): what shipped is the IBAN-failure investigation deliverable and the ticket response-time monitoring deliverable, both packaging already-run, read-only queries against DA-PAY and DA-TCK (work items W-WI-1 and W-WI-2, DONE). Actual remediation (correcting IBAN data and reprocessing failed refunds) was excluded from release scope because the environment has no write access to payment-db and no confirmed owner for a handoff to execute the fix, and because two verification obligations (VOB-R-2, VOB-U-PROCESSING-SPEED-VS-FORMAT) tied to those actions remain open — though since those actions are outside the release scope, they did not block this release. A non-critical open question (VOB-R-3 / U-FAILURE-VOLUME-SCALE) about whether the 5 known failure records represent the full failure volume does intersect the released investigation scope but was judged non-blocking.
